messages:
marta: Heads-up — console preflight flagged a save error for some routing YAML because of header tiebreaker ordering. The red banner is opaque; users don't know the minimal change to make it pass. Repro below.

marta: ```yaml
matchers:
  - type: header
    name: X-Tenant
    values: [alpha, beta]
  - type: header
    name: X-Tenant
    values: [gamma]
header_tiebreaker:
  strategy: first_match
```

raj: I hit this too. Linter currently emits "header ordering ambiguous" but the parser normalizes the matcher list which confuses the preflight vs runtime. We're basically telling the user to reorder but not suggesting how.

kevin: Proposed UX: preflight returns a list of suggested fixes (title + small patch). Console shows a diff preview and a one-click "Apply suggestion" button. No silent autosave.

aline: agree on no silent autosave. We should classify this as a suggestion (low severity) not an error. Also watch out for templated values (`{{...}}`) — autofix could break templates.

jen-product: Product here — keep the CTA minimal: Show suggestion -> Diff modal -> Apply or Dismiss. Track telemetry: suggestion_shown, suggestion_applied, suggestion_dismissed. This will help tune lint severity over time. :eyes:

raj: Implementation sketch for the server contract: preflight endpoint returns `issues: [{id, severity, message, fix: {kind: "patch", format:"yaml", body: "..."}}]`. Client can render `fix.body` as the suggested YAML. Example:```
{
  "id": "RULE_HEADER_ORDER",
  "severity": "suggestion",
  "message": "Header matcher order may affect precedence; canonicalize to merge duplicates.",
  "fix": {
    "kind": "patch",
    "format": "yaml",
    "body": "matchers:\n  - type: header\n    name: X-Tenant\n    values: [alpha, beta, gamma]\n"
  }
}
```

lint-bot: Suggestion created: RULE_HEADER_ORDER (fix available) — triggered by 2332109876. (reacted with :white_check_mark:)

kevin: Console caveats: we need deterministic parsing/printing to make diffs sensible. Using a preserving YAML lib (ruamel.yaml) would keep comments/ordering where possible, but preserving all comments across reordering isn't guaranteed. We should warn users in the modal: "This suggestion reorders matcher entries; comments may be moved."

aline: Tests: add unit tests for roundtrip + suggestion idempotency. Fuzz a few permutations of matchers, assert preflight either no-op or a single canonical fix that passes lint and runtime parse. Also add a golden file for the diff snapshot.

marta: I'll draft the PR: lint rule + tests + preflight payload. Assigning server contract to @raj and UI pieces to @kevin. I'll mark the lint as default-suggestion.

raj: One more: add feature flag `preflight_autofix_ui=true` default off for Dedicated/private customers. We don't want unexpected UX changes for them.

jen-product: Please add a short line in the release notes about suggested fixes and the telemetry we'll collect. We'll use the metrics to decide if severity should escalate to warning later.

kevin: Quick implementation checklist: server returns fixes; console renders diff modal; apply action opens a commit dialog (autosave off) — should be a change review step. Also add an analytics event for preview_opened.

marta: Thanks — I'll open the PR and ping reviewers. If anyone wants to pair on the tests, ping me.

aline: 👍 small follow-up: add an allowlist for rules that can propose fixes (no fixes for templated or binary-ish fields).

raj: Noted. I'll add contract validation to ensure `fix.format` is one of ["yaml","json"] and `fix.kind` is either "patch" or "replace".

marta: Great. I'll include examples in the PR description and a short runbook for support (how to revert suggestion applications).

jen-product: Nice work — excited to see this. :thumbsup:

kevin: cool — landing plan: feature-flag rollout to alpha, collect telemetry for 2 weeks, then broader rollouts.

marta: End of thread — will follow up in PR 2332170000.
